A louder or peak-reduced version can seem better before the actual timbral or envelope change is judged.

user_intent: Concept and listening foundation for distinguish nonlinear character from foldback artifacts.

canonical_question: I am getting this result on high notes, cymbals, or bright synths after using recognizing aliasing artifacts: “develops inharmonic fizz or tones that move downward.” What should I check first?
clarification_questions: What exactly do you want to change in the high notes, cymbals, or bright synths: onset, body, sustain, spectrum, density, peak shape, or perceived position?
Does the problem remain when the processed and unprocessed versions are closely level-matched?
Is the problem present in the source alone, or only in the full mix or after later processors?

competing_hypotheses.description: Recognizing aliasing artifacts is addressing the intended envelope or nonlinear problem and needs only a bounded amount.
competing_hypotheses.label: Hypothesis 1

competing_hypotheses.description: The audible complaint is mainly caused by level, source, performance, arrangement, timing, masking, or routing rather than recognizing aliasing artifacts.
competing_hypotheses.label: Hypothesis 2

competing_hypotheses.description: The method is plausible, but an implementation detail—gain staging, phase, detector timing, oversampling, crossover, latency, or order—is producing the unwanted result.
competing_hypotheses.label: Hypothesis 3

direct_answer: The “develops inharmonic fizz or tones that move downward” result can reflect the processor amount, gain staging, routing, source envelope, or another problem upstream. Aliasing folds generated energy above Nyquist back into the audible band, often producing inharmonic components whose motion differs from ordinary harmonics. Start diagnosis by isolating one variable: Use a rising sine or simple bright phrase at matched drive with oversampling off and on, then compare the moving high-frequency artifacts.
evidence_needed: The exact source scope, musical section, processor, routing, and current input/output level.
A synchronized, level-matched bypass or before/after comparison of the same passage.
The user’s report of what improved, worsened, or did not change.
Current Logic version and visible parameter state when exact navigation matters.
key_distinction: Aliasing folds generated energy above Nyquist back into the audible band, often producing inharmonic components whose motion differs from ordinary harmonics.
limitations: Starting values are orientations, not universal presets.
Product documentation establishes controls and stated behavior, not artistic superiority.

Exact Logic procedures remain unverified on the owner’s installed build.

A louder or peak-reduced version can seem better before the actual timbral or envelope change is judged.
A local improvement can create a new masking, headroom, phase, noise, or arrangement problem.
user_intent: Artifact diagnosis for control attack or decay without the same level threshold behavior.

canonical_question: What one-step experiment should I run with transient shaper versus compressor on a dynamic source to control attack or decay without the same level threshold behavior?
clarification_questions: What exactly do you want to change in the a dynamic source: onset, body, sustain, spectrum, density, peak shape, or perceived position?
Does the problem remain when the processed and unprocessed versions are closely level-matched?
Is the problem present in the source alone, or only in the full mix or after later processors?

competing_hypotheses.description: Transient shaper versus compressor is addressing the intended envelope or nonlinear problem and needs only a bounded amount.
competing_hypotheses.label: Hypothesis 1

competing_hypotheses.description: The audible complaint is mainly caused by level, source, performance, arrangement, timing, masking, or routing rather than transient shaper versus compressor.
competing_hypotheses.label: Hypothesis 2

competing_hypotheses.description: The method is plausible, but an implementation detail—gain staging, phase, detector timing, oversampling, crossover, latency, or order—is producing the unwanted result.
competing_hypotheses.label: Hypothesis 3

direct_answer: Use it as a bounded, level-matched experiment rather than a preset. Run this test: Level-match a small transient-shaper move against a compressor move aimed at the same audible goal. The goal is to hear attack, sustain, groove, noise, and whether quiet and loud hits respond consistently.
evidence_needed: The exact source scope, musical section, processor, routing, and current input/output level.
A synchronized, level-matched bypass or before/after comparison of the same passage.
The user’s report of what improved, worsened, or did not change.
Current Logic version and visible parameter state when exact navigation matters.
key_distinction: A transient shaper generally follows envelope change rather than only absolute level, while a compressor applies time-varying gain once its detector crosses a condition.
limitations: Starting values are orientations, not universal presets.
Product documentation establishes controls and stated behavior, not artistic superiority.
Professional and community sources are context-bound and may disagree.
Exact Logic procedures remain unverified on the owner’s installed build.
